components.css: .ds-rafters{--H:160px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,104px);gap:12px;margin:0;padding:0 14px 8px;list-style:none;background:linear-gradient(#8a847a,#2b2926) 0 0/6px 18px no-repeat,linear-gradient(#8a847a,#2b2926) 100% 0/6px 18px no-repeat,linear-gradient(#8a847a,#4d4943 45%,#2b2926) 0 5px/100% 7px no-repeat;font-family:system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-banner{position:relative;height:calc(16px + var(--H) + 86px);filter:drop-shadow(0 8px 10px rgb(0 0 0/.4))}.ds-banner-link{display:block;height:100%;color:#ede6d6;text-decoration:none}.ds-banner-link::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:1px;left:16%;right:16%;height:20px;border-inline:7px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--felt) 78%,black);border-radius:3px 3px 0 0}.ds-felt{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:16px;height:max(calc(var(--drop)*var(--H)),68px);display:flex;justify-content:center;padding-top:18px;color:var(--ink,#f3ecdc);background:linear-gradient(90deg,rgb(0 0 0/.22),transparent 16% 84%,rgb(0 0 0/.22)),linear-gradient(rgb(0 0 0/.18),transparent 28px),var(--felt);clip-path:polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,50% calc(100% - 14px),0 100%);transition:filter 150ms}.ds-felt::before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:5px 5px 17px;border:1px dashed currentColor;opacity:.6}.ds-numeral{font-family:Graduate,Rockwell,Georgia,serif;font-size:1.875rem;line-height:1}.ds-caption{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:calc(24px + max(calc(var(--drop)*var(--H)),68px));display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:2px;text-align:center}.ds-title{font-family:Graduate,Rockwell,Georgia,serif;font-size:.8125rem}.ds-meta{font-size:.6875rem;color:#aba393}.ds-value{font-weight:700;font-size:.875rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-banner-link:hover .ds-felt{filter:brightness(1.12)}.ds-banner-link:hover .ds-title{text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}.ds-banner-link:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #ede6d6;outline-offset:4px}

narrative.overview:
Every team-season is a championship banner hung in the rafters, and the ranking is the order they hang in. The ground is dim arena steel, warm charcoal and never pure black, under a single steel rod. Banners are twill felt with a chain-stitched inner border and a swallowtail hem, set in varsity block numerals. A banner's length is its score on a zero baseline, so the rafters are a bar chart that reads as a gym ceiling.

Color is encoding, not decoration. Each major league owns one felt hue (LCK royal, LPL crimson, LEC forest, LCS gold), used identically on banners, league tags, filter swatches and chart lines. Every other league hangs in neutral felt. Everything that is not a league is cream stitch thread on steel. Below the rafters sits a dense, quiet table (about 29px rows, tabular numerals, right-aligned numbers), because the table is the product and the banners only stage it.

The world explicitly refuses the dark-neon esports dashboard and the card-grid stat hub. There are no cards, no glows, no gradients other than the rod's metal and the felt's shading.
keyCharacteristics: Warm charcoal steel ground, single cream ink.
League hue is the only color, and it always means the league.
Banner length is data on a zero baseline; nothing is lengthened to fit text.
Varsity block face for names, numerals and titles; system sans for reading and numbers.
Dense, sortable, sticky-header table directly under the rafters.
Motion only conveys state change (the re-hang), and is instant under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Felt Means League Rule
rules.body: A league hue appears only where it encodes that league, and the same league always gets the same hue on every surface (banner, tag, swatch, chart line). Never use a felt for emphasis, status or decoration.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Everything that is not a league is drawn in stitch thread or faded thread on steel. There is no other accent; selected and focused states invert to thread rather than borrowing a hue.

rules.name: The Varsity Is Sewn Rule
rules.body: Graduate is for names, numerals and titles that would be stitched onto a banner. Never set paragraphs, table cells or controls in it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared (scores, z-scores, Elo, counts, years in pickers) uses tabular numerals and right alignment in tables.

rules.name: The Only Things That Hang Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to objects that physically hang or float (banners, an open dropdown). Rows, sections and controls are flat.

dos: Do set banner length from data on a zero baseline (value / max), with only the 68px numeral floor as a lift.
Do use the league's felt for banners and its line tint for any stroke or small mark, identically everywhere.
Do keep table rows near 29px, numbers right-aligned in tabular numerals.
Do draw selected and focused states by inverting to stitch thread or a 2px thread ring.
Do let the rafters scroll sideways on narrow screens rather than shrinking banners.
Do make every motion express a state change, and drop it under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use a league hue for anything that is not that league: no colored buttons, highlights, status colors or decorative accents.
Don't use pure black or neon; the ground is warm charcoal steel.
Don't introduce cards, glows, glassmorphism or gradient fills; the rod and the felt shading are the only gradients.
Don't put names or values on the felt; the felt carries only its numeral, text hangs in the caption.
Don't set body copy, table cells or controls in Graduate.
